title: Chunk Overlap (Textable, Numeric)
documentation:
## Purpose
Defines the number of tokens or characters shared between consecutive chunks when splitting a document. Overlap preserves context at chunk boundaries, reducing the risk of information loss.

## When to use
Use alongside [Chunk Size](https://capdag.com/browse/media:chunk-size;textable;numeric) on any machine that segments documents. A typical overlap is 10–20% of the chunk size. Set to 0 when strict non-overlapping segments are required (e.g., when deduplication is critical).

## Notes
Valid range: 0–500. Overlap must be less than chunk size. Larger overlaps increase index size and redundancy, which can reduce retrieval precision in embedding-based search.

## Textable
Coercion marker indicating the value is faithfully representable as UTF-8 text.
Strings are textable trivially; integers and booleans are textable via their
string form; structured values are textable when JSON-serialised. Binary blobs
(images, audio, raw bytes) are NOT textable — converting them to text requires
explicit transformation that may be lossy.

The value is faithfully representable as UTF-8 text without loss.

## Numeric
Coercion marker indicating the value supports numeric operations (addition,
comparison, ordering). Independent of `textable`; a numeric value is often
also textable (an integer is encodable as text), but neither implies the
other in general.

The value supports numeric operations.
